children: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said on Thursday that recent supply shocks have had surprisingly persistent effects and become more salient for policy.

"Our conventional view used to be that we would look through the supply shocks because tighter monetary policy is not going to have an effect on oil prices, not going to have an effect on a war, but it could slow down employment and output outcomes that we would be more concerned about," Cook said in conversation with New York Fed President John Williams at an event at the regional Fed bank.
Now, however, it is possible that the "optimal response" could be different, depending for instance on the sectors affected by the supply shocks, she said.
